newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI LEADS AFTER GIANT SLALOM FIRST RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI LEADS AFTER GIANT SLALOM FIRST RUN.

text.p: Italy's Deborah Compagnoni set herself up for a second successive victory of the season when she took the lead after the first run of a women's World Cup giant slalom on Friday.
The 26-year-old Compagnoni stormed down the Pohorje slope with a near-perfect run in falling snow to clock the quickest leg time of one minute 18.99 seconds.
Compagnoni, the reigning world and Olympic giant slalom champion, captured her maiden slalom win and first victory of the season at the second of back-to-back races at Semmering last weekend.
Switzerland's Karin Roten was second fastest on Friday through the 53 gates -- set by her coach Thierry Meynet -- in 1:19.09.
Local heroine Urska Hrovat was 0.16 seconds behind Roten for provisional third place and hoped to make her first podium finish of the winter.

Fourth after the first descent was Austrian veteran and 1993 overall world cup winner Anita Wachter (1:19.19), while Italian Sabina Panzanini -- winner of the giant slalom in Park City in November -- was fifth (1:19.40).
Current world cup leaders Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden and Germany's Katja Seizinger disappointed with 22nd and 13th places respectively in the first leg.
